recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is for FHIR-15876. Handle FHIR-37861, FHIR-55495, and FHIR-53948 separately if the work group wants broader changes to primitive-conversion semantics or example annotations.
issue_request: FHIR-15876 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core issue asking the FHIRPath page to clarify that FHIR is the namespace for FHIR types, that FHIR primitive types differ from FHIRPath system types including case, how implicit primitive conversion works, how is() differs from the then-current as() behavior, and the role of getValue().
initial_application: The issue was historically applied by git-svn commit 340c69711cee6353255046839edc4d5589876755, matching Jira's svn revision 14058 comment. That commit added the FHIR type namespace text, the FHIR-to-System mapping table, the is()/getValue() examples, and the as() example block to source/fhirpath.html. Later FHIRPath refactors kept the section and changed the old as() example terminology to ofType(), but the page still had three lowercase System.string examples.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml includes fhirpath.html as the built FHIRPath page, and source/terminologies/codesystem-fhirpath-types.xml marks the FHIRPath type code system as case-sensitive with the code http://hl7.org/fhirpath/System.String. Later related trackers FHIR-37861 and FHIR-55495 mention the same casing issue but remain Triaged, and FHIR-53948 is an unresolved broader primitive-conversion wording issue, so those issues were not separately decided here.
reconciliation: Updated source/fhirpath.html to use System.String in the is(), getValue(), and ofType() examples, matching the surrounding mapping table and case-sensitive FHIRPath type code system.
source_changes: source/fhirpath.html: changed three example type specifiers from System.string to System.String.
